newsitem.title: JAPAN: Major creditor banks accepting plan - All Corp.
newsitem.headline: Major creditor banks accepting plan - All Corp.

text.p: Troubled Japanese financial firm All Corp said on Thursday that its major creditor banks were accepting its special liquidation plan.
The president of the non-bank institution, Ubumi Sagara, told reporters that Tokai Bank Ltd had loans of 60.3 billion yen to All Corp as of the end of September 1996.

Loans from Sakura Bank Ltd totalled 26.4 billion yen and from Chuo Trust & Banking Co Ltd, 9.3 billion yen, he said. Sagara said the non-bank had loans to customers totalling 212.5 billion yen as of the end of September. He said 85 percent of this total was non-performing at that time.
A non-bank, which cannot take deposits, largely depends in its lending business on loans from banks and other financial institutions.

"Tokai Bank is mostly accepting our plan," Sagara said, adding that a few major creditors, including Sakura and Chuo Trust, had said that they would accept the liquidation plan as long as All Corp tried harder to recover its loans.
The banks are All Corp's three major creditors.
Sagara said the firm has a total of 97 creditors. The number includes 27 banks and the rest are mainly insurers and non-bank financial institutions affiliated with banks, he said.
All Corp said in a statement earlier that it planned to hold a shareholders meeting in March on the liquidation move and would then seek court protection from creditors.

Sagara said All Corp would continue operating as a credit-collecting company over the coming three years. He said it had already recovered 120 billion yen of loans under a restructuring programme started in April 1992.
He added that All Corp had already made loan-loss provisions for 121.6 billion yen of the 212.5 billion yen that remained at the end of September.
The company was established in 1977 and engaged mainly in lending, using real estate as collateral.

In the aftermath of the bursting of the late-1980s "bubble" of inflated asset prices, it said it had suffered soaring non-performing loans and the situation had worsened due to sluggish real estate markets and bankruptcies of some of its borrowers.
